effect_estimate.comment: Qualitative legal-institutional analysis with descriptive secondary regulatory statistics rather than an inferential econometric effect estimate. The paper traces how regulatory, judicial, and legislative interventions offset post-privatisation price increases and disconnections, while highlighting very low take-up of complex statutory affordability relief.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative / descriptive regulatory synthesis (no inferential numeric effect estimate reported): Privatisation in 1990 did not worsen the material position of disadvantaged consumers overall due to regulatory politics, judicial intervention, and post-1997 legislation. In water (England and Wales), real prices rose just under 40% between 1989 and 1995 and domestic disconnections for non-payment rose from around 8,000 (1989–1990) to a peak of around 21,000 (1991–1992). Judicial review in R v Director General of Water Services ex parte Oldham Borough Council (1998) ruled pre-payment Budget Payment Units (BPUs) unlawful disconnections without statutory notice, and the Water Industry Act 1999 subsequently banned domestic water disconnections for debt and water-limiting devices; however, the Act's overly complex Vulnerable Groups Regulations had a reported take-up rate of 1.4%, with only 7,693 successful applications in 2003–2004 and 9,217 in 2004–2005.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 6–9, Section 'Paying for water'; PDF pp. 12–13, Section 'Conclusions'

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 under the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework design ceiling; rated 2 because the paper directly documents concrete legal, judicial, and administrative mechanisms operating on water continuity and affordability relief (the 1998 High Court judicial review halting pre-payment BPUs, the Water Industry Act 1999 statutory disconnection ban, and administrative complexity limiting Vulnerable Groups Regulations take-up).

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines tariff/metering and rateable-value billing regimes (fees), statutory disconnection notice rules and overly complex Vulnerable Groups Regulations depressing take-up (procedural_steps), regulatory interpretation of statutory duties and non-enforcement by Ofwat (discretion), statutory vulnerable-group protections and company water charities (hardship_exception), judicial review by local authorities invalidating pre-payment BPUs (judicial_review), debt disconnections, pre-payment cut-offs, and the 1999 statutory disconnection ban (disconnection), criminal liability/licence enforcement (sanction), consumer committees and community anti-metering/anti-disconnection campaigns (participation), and post-1997 ministerial summits, social guidance, and cross-government affordability reviews (political_coordination).
